key_insight: Embedding random Fourier features into a PINN reduces spectral bias, allowing accurate capture of sharp elastic-plastic transitions in non-associative Mohr-Coulomb geomaterials.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a faster, mesh-free surrogate for geotechnical elasto-plastic analysis, potentially reducing reliance on costly incremental FEM simulations.
method: Random Fourier feature mapping is added to the PINN input layer to better represent high-frequency stress/strain variations.
A multi-objective loss enforces equilibrium, constitutive laws, and KKT conditions using FEM supervision.
Strain-adaptive sampling improves coverage of localized plastic zones during training.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark cases, FF-PINN outperformed the conventional PINN, cutting errors by up to about 66% in displacement and 27% in stress components, while converging in roughly half the training epochs.
watch_item: Performance is benchmarked against FEM data, so practical use still depends on careful training setup, loss balancing, and generalization beyond the tested Mohr-Coulomb scenarios.
paper_title: Fourier Feature Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Elasto-Plastic Analysis of Geomaterials with a Non-Associative Mohr-Coulomb Model
